title: Count Substrings With K-Frequency Characters I
summary: Given a string s and an integer k, calculate the count of all substrings in which at least one character occurs k or more times.
statement: Given a string s and an integer k, calculate the count of all substrings in which at least one character occurs k or more times.
constraints: s has 1–3,000 lowercase letters and 1 <= k <= len(s).
Count every nonempty substring in which at least one character occurs at least k times.
Different start/end positions count separately even when their text is equal.
hints: For each right endpoint, valid starts form a prefix once some frequency reaches k.
Move left until the newest character occurs fewer than k times; the number removed equals the valid-start count.
Increment the new character, shrink while its count is at least k, then add left to the answer.
Before adding, starts below left are exactly those whose window contained k copies; starts at or above left do not.
editorial: Before adding, starts below left are exactly those whose window contained k copies; starts at or above left do not.

tests.explanation: The valid intervals spell aba, abac, abacb, and bacb, for four total.
Every one of the 15 nonempty substrings contains a character once.
